correctness.rationale: For every nonterminal cleanup pass the candidate set strictly shrinks and the terminal set has size \(K\), so pass sizes are bounded by \(N,N-1,\ldots,K\). For \(K=1\), the maintained threshold lower-bound invariant forces reset to the unique active coordinate when it is encountered, so cleanup starts from a singleton. For \(K\ge2\), the stated rational recurrence has positive decreasing threshold increments and orders the prefix values so that exactly one prefix entry is removed per pass before the final \(K\)-element terminal pass. Independent exact-rational replay on boundary and interior \(N,K\) pairs reproduced the claimed pass-size sequence and count. The finite bundled verifier is corroborative, not the universal proof.
residual_risks: The result counts only step-4 comparisons in exact arithmetic and depends on Condat’s precise ordering/strictness semantics.
